failure_modes: Equating the architecture with one measure on one representation

Reading descriptive regime signatures as mechanisms; the measures detect and characterise regimes but do not by themselves explain transitions (that needs information-flow measures such as transfer entropy, perturbation experiments and longer recordings)
Transferring ant findings to AI agent swarms without re-validating what counts as an interaction there
gloss: Read a collective's behavioural regime as a configuration of how information can flow through its interactions
invariants: A regime is characterised by several representations, not one score
Signatures are reported relative to density and to a null baseline
The architecture is inferred from observed interactions, without access to any agent's internal plan
mechanism: A decentralised collective such as a {{superorganism}} processes information through its interaction network, so a behavioural regime (exploring, foraging, defending) can be described as a configuration of that network's informational architecture: the diversity, predictability and causal structure of interaction pathways. Measure it on several complementary representations, since {{representation_order}} warns that no single one is sufficient: spatial structure against a random baseline ({{spatial_divergence}}) and succession structure of interactions ({{sequence_signature}}), compared at matched density and against nulls. A regime shift then appears as a reorganisation of the architecture, for example the bifurcation, as interaction density rises, of low-entropy roaming into high-entropy trailing and low-entropy aggression. The view links micro-level interaction rules to macro-level colony states and generalises to other collectives, including networks of AI agents, where the same measures can detect which coordination regime a {{distributed_intelligence}} is in.
preconditions: Interactions between identifiable agents can be observed over time
